overview: Saint Lucia is an island country in the eastern Caribbean. Its capital is Castries. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1979. For a small country it has produced two Nobel Prize winners: the economist Arthur Lewis and the poet Derek Walcott.

geography.text: Saint Lucia is a mountainous volcanic island covered in rainforest. Its best-known landmarks are the Pitons, two steep volcanic peaks rising straight from the sea near Soufrière, which are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Nearby are bubbling sulphur springs.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical, with a dry season from December to May.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Saint Lucia parrot lives only on the island.

history.text: Britain and France fought over Saint Lucia so often that it changed hands 14 times, earning it the nickname 'Helen of the West Indies'. It became British for good in 1814. Saint Lucia became independent in 1979.

events.title: British for good
events.text: France gives up its claim to Saint Lucia.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Saint Lucia becomes independent; the same year, Arthur Lewis wins a Nobel Prize.

events.title: Nobel Prize for Walcott
events.text: The poet Derek Walcott wins the Nobel Prize in Literature.

government.text: Saint Lucia is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, with the British monarch as head of state, represented by a Governor-General. The Prime Minister leads the government.

economy.text: Tourism is Saint Lucia's main industry. Bananas were once its biggest export. The island also sells citizenship to investors.

culture.text: Saint Lucia has produced two Nobel Prize winners, the economist Arthur Lewis and the poet Derek Walcott. Its best-known landmarks are the Pitons, two volcanic peaks rising straight from the sea. Kwéyòl, a French-based Creole, is widely spoken alongside English.

items.title: The Pitons
items.text: Two volcanic spires, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Green fig and saltfish, made with green bananas, is the national dish.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Saint Lucia's Jazz Festival and the poetry of Derek Walcott.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Jounen Kwéyòl, Creole Day in October, celebrates the island's language and food.

sport.text: Cricket is the most popular sport. In 2024 sprinter Julien Alfred won Saint Lucia's first Olympic medal, a gold in the women's 100 m.

items.text: Julien Alfred won the Olympic 100 m.

didYouKnow: Saint Lucia is the only country named after a woman.
Saint Lucia has a 'drive-in volcano' at Sulphur Springs.

keyPeople.name: Derek Walcott
keyPeople.text: Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1992.

keyPeople.name: Arthur Lewis
keyPeople.text: Won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1979.
